description.narrative:
GOAL 1: Early warning and Protection of Human Rights in armed conflict and insecurity
Country Result. Human rights information and analyses are integrated in early warning and analysis systems
GOAL 2 Enhance and protect civic space and peoples participation
Country Result International, regional and national protection mechanisms are responsive to the protection needs of CSOs and individuals, particularly but not only in the context of political participation
GOAL 3: Strengthening the Rule of Law and Accountability for Human Rights Violations
Country Result: The new independent national human rights commission is established and complies effectively with the Paris Principles.
GOAL 4: Integrate Human Rights in Sustainable Development, Enhancing Equality and Countering Discrimination
Country Result: Law, policies and strategies on land and titles increasingly comply with human rights
GOAL 5: Increasing Implementation of International Human Rights Mechanisms Outcomes
Country Result. Increased engagement by Sudan with international and regional human rights mechanisms

OHCHR Sudan har bett Sida om fortsatt stöd till programmet "Enhancing Protection and Promotion of Human Rights in Sudan", som ska genomföras fram till december 2026. Stödet kommer att användas för att stärka OHCHRs samordning med FN:s humanitära landteam och humanitära kluster, med särskilt fokus på skydd av civila, konfliktrelaterat sexuellt våld och allvarliga kränkningar av barns rättigheter vilket innefattar stöd till MARA (Monitoring, Analysis and Reporting Arrangement) och MRM (Monitoring and Reporting Mechanism).
Stödet täcker genomförande av OHCHRs arbete i Sudan och kommer bland annat användas till kostnader för personal, aktiviteter såsom kapacitetstärkning av civilsamhällespartner liksom utförande av missioner. OHCHR har, efter krigsutbrottet i april 2023, intensifierat arbetet med bevakning (informationsinhämtning), verifiering (av information) och rapportering om brott mot internationell humanitär rätt och mänskliga rättigheter.
Stödet inleddes 2020 då Sida bidrog till upprättande av kontoret.

OHCHR has asked Sida for continued support for the program "Enhancing Protection and Promotion of Human Rights in Sudan", to be implemented up until December 2026. The support will be used to strengthen OHCHR's coordination with the UN humanitarian country teams and humanitarian clusters, with a particular focus on the protection of civilians, conflict-related sexual violence and serious violations of children's rights, which includes support for MARA (Monitoring, Analysis and Reporting Arrangement) and MRM (Monitoring and Reporting Mechanism).
The support covers implementation of OHCHR's work in Sudan and will be used, among other things, for costs for personnel, activities such as capacity building of civil society partners as well as the execution of missions. OHCHR has, after the outbreak of the armed conflict in April 2023, intensified the work with monitoring (information gathering), verification (of information) and reporting on violations of international humanitarian law and human rights.
The support started in 2020 when Sida decided to support the establishment of the office.

Overall assessment is that the prerequisites to carry out the mandates and programme of UN Human Rights Sudan have continued to be very challenging during the period. Risk mitigation has been put at the center of implementation, especially since the lack of security and direct presence in some areas in Sudan have merited alternative methods and priorities. Previous strategies with the expansion of remote and cross-border monitoring and verification, training of civil society and justice sector actors in human rights documentation etc, have been assessed as effective in order to reach results.
Result high-lights
1) Early warning, prevention and protection of Human Rights in situation of conflict and insecurity
Results: 1) Human rights information and analyses are integrated in early warning and analysis systems 2) Reduction in human rights violations by security forces and law enforcement agencies (result changed from: HRDDP is systematically applied when UN entities support national or regional security forces, law enforcement agencies, and non State actors).
Significant progress is reported towards this goal with the motivation that human rights information and analyses are integrated in early warning and analysis systems. Despite this not being a concrete results as per yet, an important factor is that "the data produced by UN Human Rights and its partners constitutes credible evidence for future accountability efforts".
Specifically CRSV has merited active coordination with UN partners like UNFPA, Unicef and IOM as these violations stood out in the data analysis, shaping collective advocay and humanitarian interventions. The regular reports and up-dates of the human rights situation have informed the design of early warning and prevention mechanisms as well as the production of code cables and high level advocacy. During the reporting period, the Designated Expert (DE) on Sudan of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, Radhouane Nouicer, conducted two missions related to the situation in the country.
Activities undertaken towards this goal have been to conduct systematic documentation of thousands of cases of human rights violations, including violations against the right to life, the right to freedom from arbitrary detention and torture, disappearance, sexual violence, and violations of rights to freedom of expression, peaceful assembly, and freedom of association. Violations have been committed by both parties to the conflict. Based on these findings, UN Human Rights has over the period produced 30-ish statements, briefs and reports. Findings recorded includes:
- At least 1500 unlawful killings;
- 350 unlawful and arbitrary arrests and detentions;
- 374 cases of sexual violence; and
- Contribution to the Monitoring and Reporting Mechanism on grave violations against children.
2) Enhancing and protecting civic space and peoples participation
Results: 1) International, regional and national protection mechanisms are responsive to the protection needs of CSOs and individuals, particularly but not only in the context of political participation 2) Rights-holders participate meaningfully in the design of public policy and processes in compliance with international standards.
Significant progress is reported with some listed achievements (activities) to underpin the claim. The examples include activities of the referrals of 27 Human Rights Defenders for protection services, the integration of grass root perspectives on humanitarian coordination and policy, working group on the protection of HRDs, holding 15 national and subnational human rights forums and capacity building sessions for 15 CSOs and HRDs, independent journalist trainings (23) on how to monitor restrictions on media freedom and hate speech. These efforts can be seen as contributing to the Outcomes and Results as they jointly support both protection and participation thorough the building and inclusion of local capacities.
3) Enhancing equality and countering discrimination, integrating human rights in sustainable development
Results: 1) Law, policies and strategies on land and titles increasingly comply with human rights standards, 2) National stakeholders adopt a human rights-based approach to the monitoring and evaluation of the realisation of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and are aware of their obligations regarding economic, social and cultural rights 3) National stakeholders adopt a human rights-based approach to data collection and use it when monitoring and implementing the SDGs 4) Legal and social frameworks increasingly comply with international human rights norms and standards regarding womens and girls autonomy and choice and protect them from violence.
By misstake No progress has been marked towards this goal and its results in the report. It is, however, communciated that it should be set at Significant progress. Work under this area includes development planning and having a focus on national stakeholders on SDG´s, land rights, womens and girls rights etc which often ideally needs to be governmental counterparts.
Achievements reported are limited to the three established CSO networks for the monitoring of ESCR violations. Prerequisites to work with national stakeholders under present circumstances are not in all conducive. Some key progress for the inclusion of a HRBA towards the UN Country Team and in the humanitarian response are, nevertheless, noted under this area of work. UN Human Rights reports that it contributed to key strategic documents that will shape humanitarian response at the national level in 2025. "Specifically, in Kassala, UN Human Rights played a pivotal role in advocating for and facilitating a multi-sectoral needs assessment in November 2024. This assessment, informed by vulnerability criteria and data disaggregation, marked a significant step toward aligning humanitarian responses with HRBA principles."
4) Strengthening the rule of law and accountability for human rights violations
Results: 1) Transitional justice mechanisms that conform to international human rights norms and standards, and are victim-centered, are put in place and have the capacity to deliver on their respective mandate 2) Domestic legislation and policy increasingly comply with international human rights standards 3) Judges assigned to gender-based violence cases apply national legislation in compliance with international human rights standards 4) A new independent national human rights commission is established and complies effectively with the Paris Principles 5) Increasing implementation of the International Human Rights mechanisms outcomes.
Good Progress is reported towards these results but it is clear that the conditions to work with rule of law and accountability are limited. The accountability so far concerns some initiatives trying to pave the way for transitional justice (forums and capacity building) with CSOs, legal professional organisations regional actors and the UNCT, but no real results of these efforts are yet noted. Efforts have been made advocating for the resuming of the reform process of the National Human Rights Commissions (in line with Paris principles).
5) Increasing implementation of the international human rights mechanisms outcomes.
Results: Increased engagement by Sudan with international and regional human rights mechanisms.
Significant progress is rated for this goal and its results. The rating is manly due to the consistent engagements by UN Human Rights and the High Commissioner Designated Expert for Sudan on advocacy and training sessions for CSOs, HRDs and journalists in regards to human rights mechanisms like the HR Council, Special Procedures, Treaty Bodies and Universal Periodic Reviews, resulting in the submission of an analysis on Freedom of Expression by the Sudan Journalist Syndicate to the Un Special Rapporteur. Also, UN Human Rights have ensured representation of Sudanese CSOs at the HR Council, submission of reports to these mechanisms to seek accountability.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
